subject: CloudGate temporary edge provider — EU data residency & DPA questions
messages:
From: Emma Larson <emma.larson@fineta.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: temporary edge provider (CloudGate) for EU traffic - need DPA/controls info

Hi Soojin,

Quick one — we have a short-term need to route a subset of EU customer traffic through a third-party edge provider (CloudGate) while we finish our regional infra migration. The window would be roughly Jan 5 -> Feb 2. Before we authorize any routing we need:

- Confirmation this is acceptable under Redwood's DPA / subprocessor policy
- Whether CloudGate will be added to Redwood's subprocessor roster or handled via a temporary addendum
- A short infosec package: SOC2 link, certs, IP ranges, any persistence of request/response data, KMS usage, and EU data residency guarantees
- If Redwood requires a signed addendum, we can circulate a brief notice from our side but want to minimize delays

Can you confirm next steps and who on your team we should loop in? Appreciate a checklist so our legal and security teams can triage quickly.

Thanks,
Emma Larson
Head of Infrastructure Ops — Fineta
emma.larson@fineta.com
+44 20 5555 0123

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up. Quick ack and looping in security (Ben), legal/partner ops (Marissa) and product infra (Aditya) to scope.

Initial ask from our side:
- Proposed traffic subset (percent/users/route) and whether any PII or prompts will be sent to CloudGate
- Exact start/end dates and any planned extension process
- Confirmed CloudGate contact and whether they will maintain logs or caches beyond transient forwarding

Ben/Marissa/Aditya — can you review the attached CloudGate brief and advise on a minimal approvals checklist? If Fineta needs a signed addendum we can propose a two-way temp addendum that references our DPA and limits processing to routing only.

SoojIn Lee

soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Larson <emma.larson@fineta.com>
Date: 2026-12-29T08:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary edge provider (CloudGate) for EU traffic - need DPA/controls info

Thanks — a few security checklist items from my end that we'll need answered before we can authorize CloudGate as a subprocessor (even temporarily):

1) Data types: confirm whether customer prompts, model outputs, or any user identifiers will traverse CloudGate. If prompts are routed, is there tokenization or redaction?
2) Persistence: will CloudGate persist logs, request/response bodies, or KV cache? If yes, retention period and ability to purge on request.
3) KMS: will CloudGate use its own KMS? If keys are customer-scoped (Fineta-managed) where will keys be stored (region)?
4) Access model: will CloudGate have long-lived credentials/peering or ephemeral TLS-only forwarding?
5) Network: provide advertised IP ranges and CIDR blocks, and any ASN info so we can whitelist outbound/inbound traffic.
6) Attestations: SOC2 type II report (most recent), penetration test summary, vulnerability management cadence, and contact for emergency incident response.

From a mitigation standpoint we prefer: ephemeral TLS forwarding, no persistent logs, EU-resident KMS or no KMS access, and an explicit purge window (<=72 hours) for any transit logs. Also propose a canary scope (small % of traffic or small customer cohort).

If CloudGate can provide those items we can fast-track a temporary notice entry in our subprocessor roster and a short side letter to the DPA limiting processing and duration.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Security Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Larson <emma.larson@fineta.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-30T14:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary edge provider (CloudGate) for EU traffic - need DPA/controls info

Hi Emma — looping in legal. A few notes on process:

- Subprocessor route: Redwood typically publishes subprocessor additions on our roster for notice. For short-term/ephemeral providers we can issue a temporary subprocessor addendum referencing the governing DPA instead of a full DPA amendment. That addendum would: 1) name CloudGate, 2) limit processing activity to routing-only, 3) set retention bounds and data types, and 4) set explicit start/end dates and extension process.
- SCCs / transfers: since this is EU traffic, please confirm whether Fineta requires signed EU SCCs between Redwood and Fineta (we already have SCCs in our DPA) or if you need separate SCC language for CloudGate. If CloudGate will process data outside the EEA at any time we will need to confirm transfer mechanisms.
- Signing: If you want a signed copy from Redwood, we can produce the temporary addendum draft for Fineta to countersign. Please provide the HubSpot deal ID or the legal contact for Fineta and we will pull the DPA version on file.

If possible, provide: HubSpot link, the Fineta legal contact (name/email), and the precise traffic % or customer cohort intended for routing. That will help scope the addendum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Business Affairs — Redwood Inference

From: Emma Larson <emma.larson@fineta.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, CloudGate Security <security@cloudgate.io>
Date: 2027-01-03T15:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary edge provider (CloudGate) for EU traffic - need DPA/controls info

Thanks team — answers below and attaching CloudGate package. Apologies for the delay over the holidays.

- Traffic: ~12% of EU customer routing across a canary cohort of 3 customers. No additional PII enrichment; prompts and outputs will be forwarded unmodified for routing.
- Dates: Jan 5, 2027 00:00 UTC -> Feb 2, 2027 23:59 UTC. If an extension is needed we'd provide 7 days notice and new justification.
- Persistence: CloudGate will not persist request/response bodies beyond a 72-hour transient buffer used for debugging. No KV cache persisted to disk for customer data.
- KMS: CloudGate will not have access to long-lived customer KMS keys. Any key material used for TLS is managed by CloudGate and stored in their EU KMS (key id: cg-eu-kw-09).
- Network: CloudGate IP ranges: 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.128/25. ASN: AS64599.
- Attestations: SOC2 summary attached (cloudgate-soc2-summary.pdf) and a penetration test executive summary included in the package.
- Legal contact: Fineta legal — Priya Nair <priya.nair@fineta.com>. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/54321/contact/FG-2026

Attachments: cloudgate-privacy-stmt.pdf, cloudgate-soc2-summary.pdf, fineta-temp-addendum-signed.pdf

If this satisfies Redwood's checklist we are happy to proceed with a signed temporary addendum. Please let us know, and we can coordinate the go/no-go for Jan 5.

Best,
Emma
Head of Infrastructure Ops — Fineta
